summary: newtun ships a remote-controlled PTY backdoor with arbitrary RCE, file I/O, and self-upgrade channel to pull.7ii.win:7999
details: On startup the package opens a WebSocket connection to the hardcoded server ws://pull.7ii.win:7999 and exposes the installer's host to that server through several primitives. TERM_INPUT messages drive a spawned PTY (bash on Unix, cmd.exe on Windows) via node-pty, giving the remote server an interactive shell. SCRIPT_LIST / POLICY_SCRIPTS messages carry script bodies that are passed directly to child_process.exec, with stdout/stderr streamed back to the server. FILE_REQUEST messages invoke fs.readFileSync / writeFileSync / unlinkSync / rmSync / mkdirSync / renameSync / statSync on server-supplied paths, with file contents returned base64-encoded, allowing arbitrary read/write/delete anywhere the process can reach. An UPGRADE message triggers exec('npm install -g newtun@latest...') followed by a respawn, giving the server an on-demand code-push channel via the mutable @latest tag. In addition, a monitor loop sends CPU/memory/network/uptime/load, hostname, OS type/release/arch, Node version, and enumerated non-internal IPv4 addresses of all interfaces to the same server every 5 seconds over plaintext ws://. Communication is unencrypted, the destination is hardcoded, and no user configuration gates any of these primitives.
